note: Suggested skill routes summarised from one character guide per party member. That guide is not dated within the last 60 days, so treat these as suggestions, not a current consensus. Panel names follow the in-game panel list.

builds.role: GamerGuides' character guide calls the Luminary a flexible fighter who takes part in many Pep Powers and can clear groups early with spells and greatsword skills.
builds.weapon: Greatswords are suggested for the early game because their first skills cover both group fights and bosses, while swords catch up later and can pair with a shield or [[Dual Wielding]].

order.t: Take [[Flame Slash]] in Swords so the Itemized Kill Pep Power with Erik is available.
Take [[Helichopter]] in Greatswords for group fights.
If you want a stronger single-target hit early, also take [[Cutting Edge]].
Head toward [[Unbridled Blade]] as the main boss skill; it needs one Swordmastery panel unlocked first.
Take [[Pep Up]] in Luminary so you can trigger Pep Mode on command for Pep Powers.
Work up Swordmastery toward [[Sword Dance]], which can take over from Unbridled Blade against bosses.
Once Luminary expands, take [[Charm +40]] for 10 free Skill Points.
Reset Luminary to get the spent SP back.
Take [[Gigaslash]] and [[Gigagash]] in the late game to hit all enemies.
Fill in the Strength passives, such as [[Strength +25]], ahead of the other stat panels.

skip.t: Skip [[Metal Slash]] and [[Dragon Slash]] early; they only suit metal slimes and dragon-type foes.
If points are tight late, you can pass on [[Zap]] and [[Zapple]] in favour of the Charm +40 reset.
Skip the Magical Mending panel, since the Luminary has no group heal like Multiheal to benefit from it.

tips.t: [[Pep Up]] costs 25 MP; if you would rather not spend MP, the [[Pep-Up Power-Up]] panel is suggested in any case.
[[Blade of Ultimate Power]] costs 48 MP, so it drains the Luminary's MP quickly.
[[Fullheal]] and [[Omniheal]] are worth picking up in Luminary for emergencies.

builds.role: GamerGuides' character guide calls him a fast damage dealer and thief who sets up big hits through status effects and later dual wielding.
builds.weapon: Knives are suggested to start because they have strong skills for bosses, while boomerangs suit random battles but are weak against bosses.

order.t: Take [[Half-Inch]] first to steal and to enable the Itemized Kill Pep Power once the Luminary has Flame Slash.
Head toward [[Agility +30]] in Guile for its hidden +10 SP.
Reset the tree to recover the points.
Take [[Sleeper Hit]] and [[Persecutter]] in Knives, since they work together.
Take [[Cobra Strike]] and [[Victimiser]] next; poison works on more later bosses than sleep.
Unlock [[Dual-Wielding]] in Knives as your short-term goal.
Unlock [[Divide]] in Guile next; it effectively triples Erik's damage for one turn.
Once the trees expand, take [[Critical Claim]] as a long-term staple despite its MP cost.
Take [[Dually Deadly]] in Swords to remove the offhand damage penalty, plus [[Double Down]] in Boomerangs.
Take [[Fatal Flash]] in Swords for stronger single-target and boss damage.

skip.t: Skip the early Swords skills; [[Flame Slash]] is the only one that is not situational.
Hold off on boomerangs early, as they lack boss-fighting skills.

tips.t: Use [[Divide]] with [[Half-Inch]] to triple the steal rate; [[Sticky Fingers]] raises it further after the trees expand.
[[Critical Claim]] costs 64 MP but always lands a critical hit, which helps when hunting metal slimes.
His key late skills are spread apart, so aim for an overall package until you can farm [[Seed of Skill]] items.

builds.role: GamerGuides' character guide calls her the main offensive spellcaster, with strong group damage and debuffs.
builds.weapon: Heavy Wands are suggested because Veronica is a caster and wand hits restore some MP, while whips need Strength she lacks.

order.t: Head down the Vim tree toward [[Channel Anger]], which needs four of the surrounding panels.
Take the panels on the right side on the way, avoiding [[Spooky Aura]].
After Channel Anger, take the remaining resistance passive below it.
Move to Heavy Wands for its passives rather than its skills.
Once the trees fully unlock, head toward [[Maximum MP +30]] in Vim for a free 10 SP.
Reset the Vim tree.
Rebuild it going right this time.
Head toward [[Enchanting Echo]], which needs the two panels just under [[Antimagic]].
Collect the remaining Vim spells, such as [[Kaboomle]] and [[Kafrizzle]].
Finish the rest of the Heavy Wand passives.

skip.t: Skip the Whips tree; Sylvando is the better whip user and her spells already hit groups.
Skip [[Spooky Aura]] on the way to Channel Anger.
Do not aim for [[Antimagic]] early; it only helps against heavy spellcasting foes.

tips.t: [[Channel Anger]] is a better pick than [[Ring of Ruin]], since Veronica is likely the only offensive caster.
[[Sage's Breath]] helps keep her MP up in later fights.
[[Zing Stick]] gives an extra way to revive a downed ally in emergencies.

builds.role: GamerGuides' character guide calls her the main early healer and support buffer.
builds.weapon: Wands are suggested because they allow a shield and boost Magical Mending; spears are only worth it briefly, mainly for early metal slime hunting.

order.t: If you want early spear use, take [[Thunder Thrust]] and [[Party Pooper]] in Spears.
Reset Serena once Jade joins and send her down the Wands tree.
Stack Magical Mending panels through the first portion of the game to power her heals.
Take [[Snap, Crackle, Poof]] in Wands, the suggested pick from her starting trees.
When her trees expand mid-game, take [[Channel Anger]] and [[Enchanting Echo]].
Add some Magical Might.
Take [[Hypnowhip]] mid-game only to make one [[Holier Hymns]] panel reachable.
In the final portion, return to Magical Mending.
Take both [[Holier Hymns]] panels and all the Hymns.
Take all Wands passives and [[Divine Restitution]].

skip.t: Skip the Heavy Wand tree when it opens mid-game; it offers little for her.
Skip [[Dual-Wielding]] in Wands; a single wand with a shield is suggested for defence.

tips.t: Her first group heal, [[Multiheal]], arrives at level 35, so plan around single-target healing before then.
Once you rely on [[Omniheal]], Magical Mending matters much less because it heals the party to full.
The Hymns in Harpistry become much stronger once you have the two [[Holier Hymns]] passives.

builds.role: GamerGuides' character guide calls him an early party-wide healer and buffer who sets up allies, fading somewhat later in the game.
builds.weapon: Knives are suggested after the core skills, since they lead to Have A Ball and the Chivalry tree and help set up Erik's poison and sleep combos.

order.t: Head through Litheness toward [[Hustle Dance]] as soon as he joins, taking [[Sobering Slap]] on the way.
If you want extra points, detour to [[Charm +40]] in Showmanship for 10 free SP.
Reset that tree.
Continue with the next step.
Take [[Hustle Dance]], likely your first party-wide heal.
Take [[Pink Pirouette]] and [[That's Amore]] near Hustle Dance.
Take the Knives tree, including [[Cobra Strike]], to poison foes for Erik's Victimiser.
Unlock [[Have A Ball]] in Litheness through the Knives side.
If you choose whips instead, take [[Wyrm Whip]] and [[Lash Batter]].
When Chivalry unlocks, take [[Ladies First]] and [[Finger of Justice]].

skip.t: Swords add nothing exclusive for him; only use them if no one else needs swords.
If you take [[Whipping Boy]], also take the other Whipping passives, since enemies may not target him.

tips.t: Raise his Charm to make [[Hustle Dance]] and [[That's Amore]] stronger.
Showmanship is reached through either Litheness or Whips.
[[Gold Rush]] costs 1,000 gold per use instead of MP and hits all enemies.

builds.role: GamerGuides suggests her for nearly every party lineup and calls her a physical powerhouse.
builds.weapon: Spears are suggested throughout because that tree holds her strongest single-target and critical-hit skills.

order.t: Take Strength panels for Jade.
Set Jade on the Spears tree when she joins.
Head toward [[Multithrust]] as her main attack.
Take [[Party Pooper]] as her only group attack until her other trees open.
Once her trees open, head toward [[Multifeet]] in Fisticuffs while still favouring Strength.
After Multifeet, work up Allure to [[Femme Fatale]].
Take [[Pink Typhoon]], which is required before the locked [[Pink Tornado]].
Unlock [[Pink Tornado]].
Start raising Jade's Charm for her Allure skills.

skip.t: Skip Claws; spears outclass them for her.
Stop using [[Pink Typhoon]] once you have [[Pink Tornado]].

tips.t: [[Thunder Thrust]] and [[Lightning Thrust]] are useful for metal slime grinding.
[[Belle's Bow]] from Quest 18 at +3 restores 6 MP per round; two of them give 12 MP per round.

builds.role: GamerGuides' character guide calls him a jack of all trades who buffs, debuffs, heals and deals some damage, handy in boss fights.
builds.weapon: Heavy Wands are suggested early since Claws have little until that tree expands; later you choose Claws or a return to Heavy Wands.

order.t: Take Heavy Wands first, including [[Zing Stick]] for guaranteed revives.
Take [[Benediction]] in Enlightenment to cure Curse.
Leave the rest of that tree early.
Once his trees fully unlock, pick a path: Claws or Enlightenment.
If you go Claws, take [[Rake 'n' Break]] to strip enemy buffs.
If you go Claws, take [[Hardclaw]] and [[Wild Animaul]], aiming for critical hit chance.
If you go Claws, collect all the Claws passives.
If you go Enlightenment, plan for many SP to reach [[Kacrackle]] and [[Kazammle]].
At high levels, either stay on Claws or return to Heavy Wands to build Enlightenment.

skip.t: Skip Claws and most of Enlightenment early; there is little there besides [[Benediction]].

tips.t: If you skip Claws, [[Clear Your Mind]] in Enlightenment also removes enemy buffs.
Use [[Wild Animaul]] when not chasing crits; otherwise [[Hardclaw]] keeps its crit chance across hits.

builds.role: GamerGuides' character guide calls him a versatile tank and damage dealer, especially with axe and shield.
builds.weapon: Axes are suggested because every axe skill is useful and they allow a shield; late on you can switch to greatswords for more damage.

order.t: Take the Axes tree when he joins, starting with [[Helm Splitter]] and [[Scrap Mettle]].
Take [[Parallax]] for strong single-target damage.
Take [[Axes of Evil]] for group damage, using it sparingly due to his low MP.
Take [[Hatchet Man]] for metal slimes and high-defence foes.
When Fraternity unlocks, head straight for [[Forbearance]] if you use shields.
Take [[Steadfast Forbearance]] to reduce damage taken while drawing attacks.
Late in the final part, either stay on axe and shield or switch to greatswords for more damage.

skip.t: Skip the Swords tree; it has nothing exclusive and [[Dual Wielding]] suits him poorly.
[[Defending Champion]] lasts one turn and cannot combine with Forbearance.

tips.t: In the Definitive Edition, the 10SP bonus is on [[Magical Mending +20]] in Fraternity, not [[H-Pathy]].
Pair [[Holy Impregnable]] with a [[Catholicon Ring]] +3 for near-total ailment immunity.
[[Blind Man's Biff]] deals full damage regardless of Dazzle after Quest 48.
